Senses.PreferredTarget: play the line without disturbing the clear water
AlternateTargets: handle the fishing line while leaving the clear water untouched
the line is yours to play; the unviolated clear water is distinct

Senses.Explanation: You may play the line at the rod tip; the intent that does not disturb the clear water is naturally distinct pairs skilled handling with leaving the water unviolated. Muchen places the couplet after asking whether holding or releasing is right; Hongzhi uses it after a case comment; Yongjue places it after refusing a forced division into having and not having; and Boatman Decheng says it after striking Jiashan and seeing his three nods.

EvidenceBody: Muchen places the couplet after asking whether holding or releasing is right; Hongzhi uses it after a case comment; Yongjue places it after refusing a forced division into having and not having; and Boatman Decheng says it after striking Jiashan and seeing his three nods.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The same fishing couplet follows a holding-and-releasing question, two comments, and the Boatman encounter.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The line does not prescribe literal fishing: every stored case uses it inside an address, case comment, or teacher-student encounter.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: The two coordinated clauses form one transmitted couplet; splitting them would remove the stated contrast between handling and non-violation.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: The probes retain rod, line, clear water, handling, and non-disturbance.

ModifierControls.Finding: 從君 permits the addressee to handle the line; 不犯 limits that handling by saying it does not violate the clear water.

FamilyControls.Finding: Casting or hanging a hook is a broader fishing image.
The rod tip occurs outside this couplet.
Clear waves can be scenic language without the line-handling contrast.
Throwing line and hook names a different fishing action.
